title: JSON/XML serialization, HTTP status codes, pagination, rate limits, and error contracts

objectives: Read REST success and error HTTP status codes from the official error-codes table, including 403 REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
Page SOQL results with done, nextRecordsUrl, and the query locator instead of inventing offsets.
Check remaining API capacity with the Limits resource rather than guessing daily allocations.
Treat JSON vs XML as Accept/Content-Type contracts, not as a security control.
diagnostic_question: A REST query returns done=false. Another client gets HTTP 403 with REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. What do you do next for pagination versus rate limits, and which status means created versus bad JSON?
definition: Salesforce REST API responses carry an HTTP status code and usually a JSON or XML body. Success codes include 200, 201, and 204. Errors include 400 for malformed JSON/XML, 401 unauthorized, 403 refused (including REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED), and 404 not found or sharing. SOQL queries return at most 2,000 records per synchronous batch; more rows arrive via nextRecordsUrl and a query locator. The Limits resource reports remaining allocations. ([Status codes](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/errorcodes.htm); [Query](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/resources_query.htm); [Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/dome_limits.htm))
why_it_matters: Clients that ignore done=false drop rows. Clients that retry 403 limit errors in a tight loop make the outage worse. Interviewers listen for nextRecordsUrl and REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED by name.
sixty_second_explanation: Treat every REST call like a freight shipment. The HTTP status is the stamp on the label: 201 means a new crate was created, 400 means the packing list JSON was unreadable, 403 with REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED means the dock's daily quota is blown. Pagination is the next-crate ticket: if done is false, you must present nextRecordsUrl. Rate limits are the dock quota; ask the Limits window rather than guessing the number.
deeper_explanation: Official success codes: 200 OK for GET/HEAD and some PATCH; 201 Created for POST and some PATCH; 204 No Content for DELETE and some PATCH. 300 is returned when an external ID matches more than one record. 304 is not-modified with If-Modified-Since. 400 usually means the JSON or XML body could not be understood. 401 unauthorized. 403 refused—verify permissions; if the error code is REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED you exceeded API request limits. 404 missing URI or sharing. Other codes exist in the table—do not invent meanings. ([Error codes](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/errorcodes.htm))

Query: up to 2,000 records per synchronous SOQL response; the batch can be smaller. If more remain, done is false and nextRecordsUrl / query locator fetch the next batch until done is true. Query More Results uses GET /query/queryLocator. ([Query](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/resources_query.htm); [Query More](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/resources_query_more_results.htm))

Limits resource GET /services/data/vXX.X/limits returns Max and Remaining for org limits including Daily API Requests. Exact license math is edition-specific—Needs verification in the org, do not memorize a handbook number as law.

JSON vs XML is requested with HTTP headers. Apex JSON.serialize / XML serializers are later coding detail; the contract is the wire format plus error shape. SOAP clients speak XML by definition (INT-002).

mental_model.analogy: A freight dock: HTTP status stamps, JSON/XML packing lists, next-crate tickets (pagination), and a posted daily quota board (rate limits).
useful_mapping: Limits resource → look at the quota board
error[] body → the dock's error contract, not a mystery string
where_it_breaks: Bulk API 2.0 jobs use job state APIs, not nextRecordsUrl.
Composite subrequest errors can nest—read that topic, do not assume one top-level 200 means all children succeeded without checking.
Daily allocations vary by edition—do not tattoo a number from a blog.
XML vs JSON does not bypass FLS or sharing.

teach_back_prompt: Explain 201 vs 400 vs 403 REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, then how you page a SOQL query until done is true.

review_schedule.prompt: Client retries 403 in a hot loop—what is wrong?
Two-minute interview: error contract plus pagination.

flowchart TD
  Req[REST request JSON or XML] --> St{HTTP status}
  St -->|200 201 204| Ok[Success body or empty]
  St -->|400| Bad[Malformed JSON or XML]
  St -->|401| Auth[Token problem INT-004]
  St -->|403| Lim[Permissions or REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED]
  St -->|404| Miss[URI or sharing]
  Ok --> Page{SOQL done?}
  Page -->|false| Next[GET nextRecordsUrl]

claims.claim: REST responses include HTTP codes such as 200, 201, 204 for success; 400 for malformed JSON/XML; 401 unauthorized; 403 refused including REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; 404 not found or sharing issues.
claims.validation: Status Codes and Error Responses table.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I read the HTTP status first. 201 created, 400 bad JSON/XML, 401 token, 403 maybe REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, 404 URI or sharing. For SOQL I loop nextRecordsUrl until done is true. I check Limits Remaining instead of guessing quotas.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: The error-codes table is the contract. I do not treat 200 as 'all Composite children succeeded' without reading nested results. Pagination is not OFFSET invented by me; it is the query locator. Rate-limit retries need backoff and a Limits look, not a tight loop. JSON vs XML is a header choice; SOAP is XML-only from INT-002.

terminology.plain: The stamp that says whether the HTTP trip worked and why it failed.
terminology.precise: REST response header code; body usually includes error details. Official table lists 200/201/204/400/401/403/404 and others.
terminology.example: POST sObject returns 201 with the new id.
terminology.non_example: Apex DML exception with no HTTP.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent codes absent from the table.

terminology.plain: How the packing list is written on the wire.
terminology.precise: REST supports JSON and XML. Malformed bodies commonly yield 400. SOAP is XML-only (INT-002).
terminology.example: Accept: application/json on a sandbox query.
terminology.non_example: Apex JSON.serialize as a substitute for reading HTTP status.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: GraphQL JSON which is a different API family.
terminology.boundary: Parser internals are not this lesson.

terminology.plain: The agreed shape of failure: status plus body, not a random HTML page.
terminology.precise: REST error responses typically include HTTP code and a body describing the error; REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED is a named error code on 403.
terminology.example: Client branches on errorCode REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED vs INVALID_SESSION_ID.
terminology.non_example: Parsing a Visualforce error page as REST.
terminology.boundary: Composite nested errors need the Composite topic.

terminology.plain: Getting the next crate when the first truck was full.
terminology.precise: SOQL Query: totalSize, done, nextRecordsUrl, records. Query More uses the query locator until done is true. Max 2,000 per synchronous batch, sometimes fewer.
terminology.example: Loop GET nextRecordsUrl for LAB_Item__c query.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: UI API / GraphQL cursors—verify those guides separately.
terminology.boundary: Bulk query jobs are a different paging model.

terminology.plain: The ticket printed on the last crate.
terminology.precise: String used with Query More Results / present in nextRecordsUrl to fetch the next SOQL batch.
terminology.non_example: Re-running the original SOQL with a new OFFSET you invented.
terminology.boundary: Locator lifetime/cursor caps: Needs verification in current limits docs.

terminology.precise: Org API request limits. 403 with REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED means you exceeded API request limits. Limits resource shows Max/Remaining.
terminology.example: GET /limits before a large REST test in sandbox.
terminology.non_example: Assuming unlimited REST because JSON is small.
terminology.boundary: Do not quote a handbook number as the org's allocation.

terminology.precise: GET /services/data/vXX.X/limits returns Max and Remaining for multiple org limits.
terminology.example: Read Daily API Requests Remaining in a sandbox.
terminology.non_example: Setup → Company Information as the only API for remaining calls (it may show usage; REST Limits is the API contract).
terminology.boundary: Key names can vary by version.

terminology.plain: One synchronous SOQL truck-load cap cited by the Query topic.
terminology.precise: Up to 2,000 records per Query response; batches may be smaller based on size/complexity.
terminology.example: A 5,000-row query needs at least three round trips if batches are full.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Bulk 2.0 2,000-record candidate guidance (INT-002) is about choosing Bulk, not SOQL page size.
terminology.boundary: Query Options header may change size—verify.

mechanics.failure: Dropping rows when done is false

when_to_use: When designing or debugging REST JSON/XML serialization, HTTP status codes, pagination, rate limits, and error contracts.
When a SOQL REST query might exceed one page and you must follow nextRecordsUrl.
When HTTP 403 returns REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and you must stop hot retries.
When you need Remaining API capacity from the Limits resource instead of a memorized number.
When explaining 201 Created versus 400 malformed JSON in an interview.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this REST contract lesson as Bulk 2.0 job-state documentation.
Do not invent daily allocation numbers or extra HTTP codes not in the official table.
Do not treat JSON versus XML as a substitute for OAuth (INT-004) or FLS.
Do not page events with nextRecordsUrl—that is replay IDs (INT-007).
Do not hammer production Limits or queries from this lesson.
configuration_or_code_location: Error-codes table in the REST API Developer Guide

worked_example.scenario: Sandbox client queries all LAB_Item__c rows. First response done=false. A second test org returns 403 REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. A POST of bad JSON returns 400.

decisions.decision: Loop GET nextRecordsUrl until done is true; compare count to totalSize.
On REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, stop the loop, read /limits, backoff—do not tight-retry.

configuration_or_code: Pseudocode while not done: GET nextRecordsUrl.
worked_example.output: Complete row set or a controlled pause on limits.
verification: Client log shows multiple query locators when done started false.
worked_example.self_explanation: Pagination and limits are different stamps on the same dock.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable sandbox; Workbench or a small Apex/HTTP client; LAB_Item__c or Account.
steps: Run GET /query?q=SELECT+Id+FROM+Account (or LAB_ object) and note done, totalSize, nextRecordsUrl if present.
If done is true, document that paging was unnecessary; optionally insert enough LAB_ rows in sandbox to exceed one page and repeat.
GET /limits and record Daily API Requests Remaining (do not publish the number as a universal constant).
Write a unit-test style assertion in a scratch class: if status == 403 and body contains REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED then retrying immediately is forbidden.
guided_completion: If you ignored nextRecordsUrl when done was false, you failed pagination.
If you copied Remaining as 'all Salesforce orgs have this many calls,' you invented an allocation.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Map 201 vs 204 vs 400 to POST create, DELETE, and bad JSON using the official table.
evidence: Screenshot or log of a query JSON with done field.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Do not leave a paging loop against production.
hands_on_lab.limitations: May not exceed 2,000 rows in a tiny playground; then document the contract anyway.

decision_table.signal: SOQL REST response has done=false and nextRecordsUrl.
decision_table.choose: GET the nextRecordsUrl / query locator until done is true.
decision_table.not: Treat the first page as the full result set.

decision_table.choose: Halt hot retries; inspect Limits Remaining; backoff; reduce chattiness or use Bulk (INT-002).
decision_table.why: The error-codes table says API request limits were exceeded.

decision_table.choose: Fix JSON/XML serialization and Content-Type; read the error body.
decision_table.not: Assume 401 and rotate OAuth first without reading the body.

decision_table.signal: You need remaining API capacity in an integration dashboard.
decision_table.not: Hard-code a blog's edition number as the org quota.
decision_table.why: List Org Limits is the API contract; allocations are org-specific.

decision_table.choose: Expect 201 Created (per table) and parse the id from the body.
decision_table.not: Require 204 No Content for a create.
decision_table.why: 201 is the documented success code for POST creates.

limitations: Not a full HTTP code encyclopedia beyond the table.

interview_questions.question: Walk through JSON/XML, HTTP status codes, pagination, and rate limits on Salesforce REST.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Status first: 201 created, 400 bad JSON/XML, 401 token, 403 maybe REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, 404 URI/sharing. Page with nextRecordsUrl until done. Read Limits Remaining.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat the error-codes table as the contract. I never invent codes. Pagination is the query locator, not OFFSET folklore. Rate limits are not Apex governors. JSON vs XML is headers, not security.
interview_questions.example: Sandbox query of LAB_Item__c that spans two pages plus a 403 lab org.

interview_questions.question: What is the REST error contract you actually code to?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: HTTP status plus a body that often includes error codes such as REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Clients branch on those codes.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I log status and errorCode, never tokens. 400 means fix serialization. 401 goes to INT-004. 403 splits permission versus limits. I will not scrape Visualforce HTML.
interview_questions.example: Client switch on errorCode after a failed PATCH.

interview_questions.question: Your ETL downloaded 2,000 Accounts but Salesforce has 9,000. Diagnosis?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Almost certainly done=false was ignored. Follow nextRecordsUrl until done is true and compare to totalSize.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Query topic caps a synchronous page around 2,000. I check sharing next if counts still differ. I do not switch to Metadata API. If volume is huge, consider Bulk query (INT-002) instead of endless REST pages during business hours.
interview_questions.example: Nightly extract that always stops at 2,000.

interview_questions.question: Integration gets 403 after a marketing burst of REST calls.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Read the body for REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, GET /limits, stop the burst, backoff, consider Bulk or fewer chatty calls.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Tight retries make Remaining worse. I separate permission 403 from limit 403. I will not quote a fake 100,000 as every org's cap. INT-002 may say this job should have been Bulk 2.0.
interview_questions.example: Campaign sync that fired one REST POST per lead until HTTP 403.

interview_questions.question: POST returns 400. Partner swears JSON is valid.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Compare Content-Type, encoding, and the official field names. 400 means the platform did not understand the body.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I capture raw request (redacted) in sandbox. Trailing commas, extra wrappers, or XML sent as JSON are common. I do not rotate the named credential first unless the status is 401.
interview_questions.example: Extra data wrapper around sobject fields.

interview_questions.question: DELETE returns 204 but the UI still shows the row.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: 204 means the HTTP delete succeeded; the UI may be cache, sharing, or a different org. Do not treat 204 as failure.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I requery with REST, check recycle bin, and confirm the Id. Pagination is irrelevant here. If they wanted 200 with a body, they misread the table.
interview_questions.example: Workbench DELETE of a LAB_ row still visible on an old list view.

interview_questions.question: How should a client combine pagination and rate limits?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Page until done, but watch Remaining and status. If 403 limits, persist the locator if still valid, wait, resume. Do not invent locator lifetime.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I would Needs-verify query locator expiration in current limits docs rather than guess. For very large extracts I prefer Bulk 2.0 query so I am not holding many REST cursors during the day.
interview_questions.example: Multi-hour Account extract with Limits checks every N pages.

interview_questions.question: Teach the freight-dock analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Stamps are statuses, packing lists JSON/XML, next-crate tickets pagination, quota board Limits. It breaks for Bulk jobs and nested Composite errors.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map 201/400/403, then say 404 can be sharing, not a missing dock. I will not paint a fake daily number on the quota board, and I will not treat Bulk job state as nextRecordsUrl pagination.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard a two-page Account query plus a 403 REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
